description: Wordle online free: guess the five-letter word in six tries. Green means right letter, right place; yellow means right letter, wrong place.
lede: Five letters, six guesses, and three colours. Type a word and the tiles light up: green means the letter is right and in the right place, yellow means the letter is in the word but in the wrong place, and grey means it is not in the word at all. Every answer is a common word you already know — the challenge is finding it before the six rows run out.

p: Press Start guessing and type any five-letter word — either on your keyboard or by tapping the letters on the screen — then press Enter. The tiles flip over one by one: green for a letter that is right and in the right place, yellow for a letter that is in the word but sitting in the wrong spot, and grey for a letter that is not in the word at all. The keyboard colours itself the same way, so you can see at a glance which letters are still worth trying.

You have six rows, which means six guesses. Guess the word and you win; use all six rows without finding it and the word is revealed. A new word is picked for every game, so no two games are ever the same.

The colours are the whole game, and they follow one rule: green beats yellow, and a letter is only ever marked as many times as it appears in the answer. If you guess a letter twice and the answer has it once, only one tile turns yellow — the other stays grey. So a yellow tile means that exact letter is in the word, somewhere, and you still have to find where.

sections.h: From a lockdown pastime to a daily ritual
p: Wordle was made by Josh Wardle, a software engineer from Wales, as a gift for his partner, who loved word games. He built it in 2021, first for just the two of them, then for friends and family — and one word a day, shared with everyone, was the rule from the start. It spread by word of mouth through late 2021, and The New York Times bought it in January 2022.

The magic was the constraint: one puzzle a day, the same word for everyone, and a grid of green, yellow and grey squares that players could share without spoiling the answer. This version keeps that spirit with a new common word every game, so you can play as many rounds as you like.

sections.h: Tips for finding the word faster
ol: Start with a word full of common vowels and consonants, like CRANE or SLATE: it tells you the most about the answer in one guess.
A grey letter is information too. Cross it off and never spend a guess on it again — the keyboard greys it out for you.
Yellow means move the letter, not drop it. Try it in a new spot before you give up on it.
If you have two yellows, try a word that puts both of them in new places at once — it tests two ideas in one guess.
With two guesses left, stop guessing wild words and use what the colours have told you: every green stays, every grey goes, every yellow moves.

faq: How many guesses do I get?
Six. Each row is one guess, and the game ends when you find the word or the sixth row is filled.
Green: the letter is right and in the right place. Yellow: the letter is in the word but in the wrong place. Grey: the letter is not in the word at all.
Why did my guess not submit?
Two reasons: either the row is not full yet, or the word is not in the word list. Only real five-letter words can be submitted.
Are the answers always common words?
Yes. Every answer is a common, everyday word — no obscure words, no proper names, no plurals with an S tacked on.
